summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, vasculitis, POTS, and malabsorption was readmitted two days after discharge due to severe epigastric and right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and vomiting triggered by eating a small amount of food. She had persistent dry heaves and was unable to tolerate oral intake initially. Imaging showed no acute abdominal process, including no evidence of pancreatitis or obstruction. She was managed with IV pain control and anti-nausea medications, then gradually advanced to a regular diet. Methotrexate was administered after confirmation with her PCP, despite a skin biopsy not showing vasculitis. Constipation was addressed with a PR regimen and oral laxatives. Her anxiety and orthostatic hypotension were managed with continued home medications. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with adjusted doses of escitalopram and betaxolol, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
